title: A nonprofit and a company under the same people
question: Which City-funded nonprofits have officers or key employees who own a business, or a related company on their tax return, that the City or the nonprofit itself pays?
finding: 2 City-paid companies are declared as related corporations on the tax returns of City-funded nonprofits (apart from 63 related housing partnerships, which are in the first screen). 0 more row(s) rest on a name: a person on a funded nonprofit’s return has the same rare name as the registered owner of a business, with a second link (same paying department, same address, or the business on the nonprofit’s contractor list). 3 name match(es) whose only second link is a shared paying department are counted but not listed, because a department that pays hundreds of parties is too weak a link to name a person on. 5 name matches to City-paid businesses with no second link are not shown, nor are 6 businesses registered at a nonprofit’s address that neither the City nor the nonprofit is recorded as paying, nor 5 partnerships of the nonprofit itself that are registered in an officer’s name. The largest declared company: Caritas Management Corp (Mission Housing Development Corp.), $3,677,050.
how: Part one: every corporation or trust that a profiled, City-funded nonprofit lists on Schedule R Part IV of its tax return, where the same name is a City payee since fiscal 2019. Part two: officers, directors and key employees on those returns whose name is rare (the test used in the site’s “People and roles” page) and is the ownership name of exactly one owner in the business registry; a row is shown only with a second, independent link, and rows already in the insider-contractors screen of the site’s “People and roles” page are left out.
limits: A related company on Schedule R is disclosed and common: property-holding companies, thrift shops, social enterprises and management companies. The point for a reader is whether the City knew the two were one group when it paid both. Part two is a name match on a person and may be wrong even with a second link; The conflict rules that apply depend on votes and contracts not in these files. The registry does not name officers, so a company run but not owned by an officer is missed; permits that a nonprofit’s work depends on could not be tied to officers from the files on disk.
